items.summary: AI Gateway Production Index — October 2026 Every month, AI Gateway routes tens of trillions of tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage actually looks like in today's enterprise, and we publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from July , August , and September . October 2026 summary Open-weight models now process more than seven in ten gateway tokens and account for nearly one in four dollars. Their share of spend has more than quadrupled since June. September’s gateway spend was about 13 times December’s, while the average price per token was 47% lower. Almost one in three teams changed their most-used lab in September, an index record. Nearly 70% of September’s gateway spend on Chinese models went through US-based providers, up from less than 10% in December. Jev was the fastest-adopted model in AI Gateway history, reaching 35% of paid teams in its first two weeks, but it accounted for just 0.27% of gateway spend over that same period. Opus 5.5 took more than one in ten gateway dollars in its own first two weeks, the largest spend share of any September model launch. Frontier spend up 900%, spend share down 22% In August, open-weight models processed the majority of AI Gateway token volume for the first time. The money is now following. Open weight’s share of spend has more than quadrupled over the last three months, from one in twenty gateway dollars in June to nearly one in four in September. Open weight's growth is coming from both ends of its price range, and it mirrors the wider gateway. The cheapest models drive token growth, while the expensive models drive spend. Led by Kimi K3, models priced at least four times the open-weight average cost per token accounted for about two-thirds of the increase in open-weight spend. In contrast, DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash alone processed nearly half of all September tokens but took just 2.6% of spend. Its price per token was about a fifth of the open-weight average. Customers are increasing budgets on both sides of the market. Since December, spend on frontier models has grown tenfold; spend on open-weight models has grown more than seventyfold. In September, 68% of teams that put more money into open-weight models did the same for closed-weight models. And more than two in five teams already paying for frontier models spent more on them than in August, the highest share this year. Spending on the frontier is still growing, but spending on alternatives is growing faster. A company can spend more with a frontier lab while relying on it for fewer workloads, so the lab gets more money, but a smaller part of the customer’s business. AI spend increases 13x while the cost per token halves Market share is changing hands inside a market that is getting much bigger and cheaper. September's gateway spend was about 13 times December's, an increase of 1,180%, while the average price per token fell 47%. The median paid customer active in both December and September more than doubled its spend. Teams are spending more, but labs have to keep winning their business. In September, nearly one in two teams changed their most-used model. And almost one in three changed their most-used lab, an index record. Even teams with lower token volumes use a wide mix of models. Since December, teams that processed at least 10 million tokens over that period used an average of 15 different models. The average rose to 26 for teams processing at least 100 million tokens, and 42 for those processing at least a billion. The model is becoming a replaceable part of a much larger investment. Companies can continuously improve their AI products and workflows while changing which models power them. They can spend more on AI without becoming more dependent on any one lab. Chinese models are big business for American providers More than two-thirds of September’s gateway spend on Chinese-origin models went to US-based providers, up from less than a tenth in December. The Chinese lab builds the model; the American provider runs it and sells access. DeepSeek’s models processed 58% of all gateway tokens for 6.6% of spend. More than four in five of those tokens were served by DeepSeek itself, yet two in five dollars spent on its models went through US-based providers. Moonshot AI, the Beijing-based lab behind Kimi, accounted for 3.6% of gateway tokens and 13.2% of spend in September. US-based providers served nine in ten of those tokens. Z.ai, also based in Beijing and the creator of GLM, accounted for 7.2% of all tokens and 4.5% of spend. US-based providers served seven in ten. Customers can use Chinese models through access sold by American providers. For teams that put more money into Chinese models in September, an average of 53% of their spending on those models went through US-based providers and 41% through China-based ones. The same Chinese model can compete with US-based models while generating revenue for US-based providers. September model launch scorecard: Jev, Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Whether a model launch is successful depends on what you measure: how broadly it’s tried, how much usage and spend it receives, or what share of its initial users return. We ranked every model launch in September with at least two weeks of data by these metrics; the tables show the top ten for each. The full scorecard is at the end of the report. Jev is the most-adopted and most-called model In its first two weeks, Jev reached more than a third of paid teams, nearly double the reach of Sonnet 5.5 in second place. This is the fastest adoption of any model in AI Gateway history. Jev also received the most requests of any model in September, even though it launched halfway through the month. Of the teams that tried Jev in week one, 55.6% returned in week two, the fifth-highest retention rate. Jev is a decision model. Compared with typical language-model requests, a Jev request is faster, cheaper and uses a fraction of the tokens. So although its adoption was fast and broad, it accounted for just 1% of the month’s tokens and 0.15% of spend. In September, Jev quickly became a popular model for production while remaining a tiny part of the inference bill. Opus 5.5 takes more than one in ten gateway dollars The launch that received the most dollars was Opus 5.5, with more than twice the share of any other September launch, followed by GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash. Opus 5.5 caught on quickly, with almost nine in ten dollars coming from teams already using Opus 5. Existing customers were trying the new release while the wider Opus family was losing market share. Across all versions, Opus accounted for almost a third of gateway dollars in September, down from one in two in August. Anthropic’s overall share fell below half of total gateway spend for the first time, dropping from 63.7% to 43.9%. Luna brought users back; Astra brought spend GPT-6 Luna reached nearly three out of every twenty paid teams in its first two weeks, in third place behind Jev and Sonnet 5.5. But its return rate was the highest of the month; almost two-thirds of the teams that tried it in its first week came back in the second. GPT-6 Astra reached a smaller audience but took more budget. In its first two weeks, it accounted for about one in twenty gateway dollars; Luna accounted for less than one in a hundred. Luna reached almost three times as many teams while Astra captured more than five times the share of spend. OpenAI is attracting more customers with Luna, but capturing far more money with Astra, even though fewer teams use it. Average price per token is estimated spending divided by token volume. Open-weight classifications follow the current AI Gateway model list, a broader definition than in earlier reports. items.title: Vercel for Enterprise
items.summary: AI adoption in the enterprise is growing rapidly, and expanding beyond engineering users. In the last three months, token usage by enterprise companies on AI Gateway has quadrupled, and OpenAI recently reported that from August 2025 to June 2026, non-developer Codex users grew 189x. Our customers call these builders citizen developers. They know their part of the business better than anyone else, and with AI they can create the software they need to ship work faster and deliver better customer experiences. Building has never been easier, but that also means that control and governance have never been harder. Employees are using AI tools whether they are approved or not , and if a citizen developer vibe codes a login page incorrectly, private data can reach the public internet. Enterprise leaders have to figure out how to let everyone build, without giving up security or control. Enterprise Apps and Agents We built Enterprise Apps and Agents to solve these challenges at Vercel, and in June, we made it available to our customers. Enterprise Apps and Agents is a central control plane for governing every builder, app, agent, token, and dollar. Today, we are expanding the platform: Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) on AWS is generally available, giving you the full Vercel developer experience, while keeping compute and data inside your AWS boundary. Enterprise-Managed Authorization through Vercel Connect is launching in public beta, giving agents the ability to access connected services on behalf of employees through your IdP. A single control plane for governing enterprise AI Enterprise Apps and Agents gives you a single deployment destination for both engineers and citizen developers, with central governance over access, providers, models, data retention, token budgets, integrations, and policies, managed through your existing IdP. Vercel centralizes AI governance so that company policies can be applied consistently across control domains. Control domain Vercel controls Deployment governance Enterprise Managed Users and RBAC Access governance Vercel Passport , Deployment Protection , and Vercel Firewall Integration and data governance Vercel Connect and Enterprise-Managed Authorization Model and token governance AI Gateway , including US-only inference and budget controls Apps and agents run on the same infrastructure that powers billions of production deployments, and Vercel gives you a single place for observability and security monitoring across every project, through analytics , audit logs , and the Security Dashboard . Secure Compute provides private connectivity to enterprise systems, while BYOC on AWS lets your application functions run in your own AWS account under your permissions and network controls. Deployment governance Citizen developers and engineers use different tools. A marketer might use ChatGPT to build a landing page, an analyst might use Claude Code to run queries and build a report, and an engineer might use Codex, OpenCode, or fx. No matter the harness, Vercel gives you a single deployment target, and connects to your existing IdP, so you can control who creates deployments. How Klaviyo's built a secure internal app platform Before Vercel, shipping a simple internal app at Klaviyo took two weeks of chasing IT, opening tickets for engineering, and following up with the platform team. They built an internal app-building platform on top of Enterprise Apps and Agents, and now anyone in the company can deploy an idea in three minutes. In their first two weeks on Vercel, 512 employees deployed 356 apps. Access governance Controlling who can deploy doesn't protect the apps, agents, and data that make it into production. On Vercel, you can configure every deployment to be private by default, and with Vercel Passport, you can require employees to authenticate through your IdP before they can access internal apps. Integration and data governance Agents are only useful when they can access your systems and data, but that often means using long-standing environment varibles with wide-ranging permissions to your CRM, databases, Slack, and other systems. Vercel Connect implements connectors with scoped access, and mints tokens for each agent task, meaning agents only access the specific context they need for the job. And now, with Enterprise-Managed Authorization, when employees sign into Vercel through your IdP, agents can use connected services automatically, without a separate authorization prompt. Connect also integrates with Passport, so individual employee permissions also apply at the integration and data layer. If someone can't see data in a source system, they can't access it through an app or agent either. Model and token governance The average enterprise company using Vercel AI Gateway routes across 17 different models. Without a model router, that would require integrating with multiple separate providers, spreading API keys and budget management across platforms. AI Gateway gives you access to hundreds of models through a single API, with no markup on cost, and Zero Data Retention keeps your data from being stored or trained on. You can also elect to route through US-only providers to maintain compliance. How Mercor manages model governance at scale Mercor connects AI labs with subject-matter experts who help train and evaluate models. Their engineers need access to hundreds of models to enable that work, but before migrating to Vercel, access was spread across direct integrations and third-party routers, making stolen credentials a huge risk, and token spend impossible to manage. They moved their model routing to AI Gateway, and now engineers can access hundreds of models with a single, expiring secret, and they can set budgets per person or project. In their first 10 days on AI Gateway, they processed 63 billion tokens without hitting any rate limits. Centralized visibility and security Vercel Observability gives you a single view for app and agent telemetry across every project, so you can easily manage performance and troubleshoot problems for both internal tools and customer-facing products. The Security Dashboard flags risks across your team and apps, including missing MFA, unprotected preview deployments, long-lived credentials, and framework vulnerabilities. Each finding links to the settings needed to fix it. Bring Your Own Cloud on AWS BYOC on AWS is generally available . With BYOC, application functions execute in your AWS account, within your security and network boundaries. Meta Superintelligence Labs runs on Vercel via BYOC, giving its AI teams the ability to test and deploy ideas quickly, inside their own AWS environment. Leaders at Meta said that in their first week on Vercel, they shipped a month worth of work. From idea to global scale on one platform Vercel let's everyone in your company build safely, and makes it easy for engineers to ship the best ideas at global scale, all on a single platform. That is how we built Vertex, our customer support agent. We were previously using a vendor, but it couldn't answer all of our customers questions. When our support team built agents and skills to cover the gaps and increase our responses times, and we realized they had laid the foundation for the experience we wanted to deliver directly to our customers. Our GTM engineering team took that foundation and made it production ready with evals and model failover. Today, Vertex handles 91% of our customer support cases autonomously, processing thousands of tickets a week, and it runs on the same platform where the idea started. Ship your best ideas, securely Contact sales to learn more about enterprise governance on Vercel and get a custom demo of the platform. items.title: Backends on Vercel: Python, containers, and Daemons
items.summary: Last year, we expanded zero-config support for Python and TypeScript backend frameworks. By this summer, developers could deploy their frontend and backend together with Vercel Services and coordinate background work with queues and durable workflows . Today at Vercel Ship in San Francisco , we are expanding the backend workloads you can run on Vercel. Python on Vercel is now generally available, container support in Vercel Functions enables custom runtimes and system libraries, and we are introducing Vercel Daemons in Public Beta for background workers that pull work and stay running between jobs. Python is now generally available You can build your backend in Python with the Vercel infrastructure and development experience you know from your frontend, including local development, previews, and production deployments. Frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, and Django run on standard CPython with your PyPI dependencies, while Vercel handles framework detection, builds, and scaling. Already, 150,000 teams run Python backends on Vercel, including engineers at OpenAI, Polymarket, and Exa. SDKs for Python let you use Vercel products from your application, whether you’re storing files in Vercel Blob , sending background jobs to Vercel Queues , coordinating durable steps with Vercel Workflows , running untrusted code in Vercel Sandbox , or streaming model responses and handling tool calls with the AI SDK for Python . Delphi , which builds AI digital minds from books and talks, moved its Python backend from AWS ECS to Vercel. With ten engineers and no dedicated infrastructure role, the team ships to production more than 100 times a day and uses Queues to handle background jobs. Visit the Python knowledge base for framework details and examples. Applications in any language with containers The Vercel container runtime lets you deploy applications written in any language, packaged with the OS libraries and executables they need. Since container support entered Public Beta, 5,000 teams have shipped 150,000 container deployments on Vercel. Containers deploy as Vercel Functions on Fluid compute, scaling with traffic and using Active CPU pricing , which doesn’t charge for idle time spent waiting for API responses, database queries, or LLM inferencing. Vercel Services lets you develop and deploy your backend alongside your frontend, while Vercel CDN serves traffic on your domains, Vercel WAF protects it, logs help you investigate issues, and rollbacks restore earlier deployments. For example, take a video app that uses a container for background processing, preparing a playback copy and thumbnail for each uploaded clip. This Dockerfile packages the Python processor, its dependencies, and ffmpeg to run with Daemons: When you deploy through Git or the Vercel CLI, Vercel builds the image and stores it in your Vercel Container Registry . Read our containerized Functions deployment guide to get started. Background workers with Vercel Daemons Vercel Daemons lets you deploy containers as continuously running background workers on Fluid compute. You choose the number of instances in each region, and Vercel maintains that capacity by restarting processes when they exit or crash. Daemons launches with support for pull-based workloads, where your code requests work from another system and processes it as it becomes available. That could mean consuming queue messages or fetching pending jobs from a database. In our example, Daemons runs the video processor continuously as it pulls jobs from Vercel Queues . In vercel.toml , define the Next.js frontend, route requests to it, and add the processor using Dockerfile : Follow the Daemons deployment guide to add a background worker to your Vercel project. Run your backends on Vercel We’re continuing to invest in backend support so more of your existing application can run on Vercel, using the languages, dependencies, and execution patterns it needs. items.title: Python on Vercel is now generally available
items.summary: Python on Vercel is now generally available. Build and run Python applications with the frameworks, libraries, and tools you already use. Vercel automatically detects supported frameworks and configures the build and deployment. Your applications run on Fluid compute, which manages concurrent requests and scales with traffic. Idiomatic Python SDKs let you work with storage, queues, durable workflows, and AI models directly from Python. For full-stack projects, the Python backend and frontend share a workflow for local development, preview deployments, and production releases. Our goals for Python on Vercel Ten months ago, we set out to make Vercel the best place to build and run Python applications . We wanted the experience to fit how Python developers already work, with three goals guiding our decisions: Idiomatic Python SDKs. Working with Vercel infrastructure should feel familiar to Python developers, with APIs that use type annotations, async / await , and context managers. A shared workflow for both the frontend and backend. Python applications often include a JavaScript frontend, so developers should be able to run both locally, review them in the same preview deployment, and release or roll them back together. Compatibility with the Python ecosystem. The runtime should use CPython, the standard Python interpreter, on Linux to preserve compatibility with the packages and tools Python developers already rely on. The first test of those goals is what happens when you deploy a Python application on Vercel: its framework, dependencies, and project structure should guide how it’s built and run. Deploying Python applications on Vercel We’ve worked to make Python feel native on Vercel. Vercel reads your project’s dependency files, including those managed by uv , and automatically detects frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, Django, and FastHTML. Framework defined infrastructure configures builds and request routing, with framework-specific support for serving static assets through the CDN. For applications with a frontend, Vercel Services brings both parts into one project. Running vercel dev starts them together, and shared previews let you test backend changes with the frontend that uses them. For long-running workers that pull jobs from queues or databases, Vercel Daemons keeps your containers running with your Python code along with any of its packages, and system dependencies. Python SDKs for Vercel infrastructure A Python backend might need to store files, send messages, run durable workflows, or call AI models. We’ve built Python SDKs for these tasks, with APIs that follow the conventions of the language: These SDKs work alongside your framework and libraries, and the example below shows how they connect within a full-stack application. Start building with Python on Vercel Whether you’re starting a new project or deploying existing code, the framework guides cover setup and deployment on Vercel. For a guided full-stack project, the Python on Vercel course walks through building a FastAPI backend and Next.js frontend, then deploying them together with Services. To show how these pieces work together, I built a collaborative web application to create and browse Python notebooks. It lets people create their own notebooks, publish them for others to browse or fork, and work with an AI assistant to write and run Python code. The application pairs a Vite frontend with a FastAPI backend and uses PostgreSQL for notebook source and chat history. Services keeps the frontend and backend in one deployment, with the frontend served through the CDN. Here’s how the main parts connect: Editing and running code: When a signed-in user opens their notebook in the editor, FastAPI creates or reuses a Vercel Sandbox running Jupyter, keeping user code isolated from the application backend. The browser connects directly to Jupyter, while mounted Drives provide the Python dependencies and workspace files. Saving and publishing: The browser periodically sends the current notebook to FastAPI. FastAPI saves the source in PostgreSQL, renders changes as HTML, and uploads the result to Blob, so people can read published notebooks through the CDN without starting a Python kernel. Sharing updates: After publishing a change, FastAPI sends a message through Vercel Queues. Each backend instance with connected browsers receives the notification and sends updated notebook listings over WebSockets, so people see changes without reloading. Assisting with code: The agent uses AI SDK for Python and runs inside Vercel Workflows, which saves execution state and retries failed steps. Chat history stays in PostgreSQL, while notebook editing and execution tools work through the connected browser, which sends results back through FastAPI to resume the workflow. The source code on GitHub includes the complete application and its deployment configuration. You can use it to explore these integrations or as a starting point for your own Python application. Investing in the Python community Last December, the Gel Data team, led by me and Elvis Pranskevichus, joined Vercel to build Python support and continue our open-source work. At the same time, we announced our sponsorship of the Python Software Foundation and committed to funding one year of Serhiy Storchaka’s CPython maintenance through the foundation. Serhiy has authored over 600 commits to CPython’s main branch so far in 2026. We also sponsored PyCon US and EuroPython this year, where the team and I met Python developers and heard where they were getting stuck. Those conversations help us figure out what to fix next. We also published PEP 827 , which, if accepted, would add type manipulation features that could help frameworks such as FastAPI offer simpler APIs with less boilerplate and more precise type checking. What’s next for Python on Vercel We’re continuing to improve Python SDKs, runtime performance, and development workflows for both people and coding agents. If you run into a deployment issue or find something missing in the Python SDKs, share your feedback in Vercel Community so the team can use it to guide that work. items.title: Python on Vercel is now generally available

Build APIs, full-stack applications, and AI agents with native Python SDKs and a shared development and deployment workflow for your Python backend and JavaScript frontend. Python framework and runtime support Vercel handles the infrastructure so you can focus on your application: Automatic framework support: FastAPI, Flask, and Django applications are automatically recognized and configured, with framework-specific support for serving static assets through the Vercel CDN. Native Python runtime and tooling: Vercel runs CPython on Linux and supports uv and pyproject.toml for dependency management. Compute for APIs and workers: Scale request-driven applications with Fluid compute and run long-running pull-based workloads with Vercel Daemons. Native Python SDKs Within your application, Python SDKs let you build agents, run untrusted code, and orchestrate durable workflows. Sandbox : Give your application or agent an isolated Linux VM on demand. AI SDK for Python (Beta): Generate or stream model responses and call tools. Get started with uv add ai . Workflow SDK for Python (Beta): Persist execution state and retry failed workflow steps. Queues (Beta): Send and receive messages for background work. Connect : Obtain credentials for calling external APIs. Blob : Upload and retrieve files in object storage. Use the SDKs individually or combine them in the same Python application. Your frontend and backend, together For full-stack applications, Vercel Services allows you to deploy your frontend and backends together in one project, with shared previews and atomic deployments and rollbacks. Within that project, you can view logs by service and connect backends privately through service bindings. For a frontend in frontend/ and a FastAPI app defined in backend/main.py , add this vercel.toml at the repository root. Requests under /api/ reach matching FastAPI routes with the path unchanged, while other requests reach the frontend. Run both services locally with vercel dev , then deploy them together from the same repository. Read the Python documentation to get started. Read more

items.titleJa: 35日でフロントエンドの基礎を完全に理解する #9 - コンポーネント分割（props・emit・slots）
items.summaryJa: コンポーネント分割の基本として、 props で親から子へデータを渡し、子は受け取ったデータを書き換えず、イベントを emit して親へ知らせる一方向の流れが解説されています。slot を使えば、外枠となる部品に親が中身を差し込むことができ、再利用性と見通しの良さが向上します。実例として、LikeButton によるいいねのカウントは親が count を持ち、子は押されたことだけ伝える構成、Panel の中身差し込み、ProductCard の props 用例が挙げられています。次回は v-model を使ったフォームへの応用が紹介されます。

items.summary: Gemini 4 Argon from Google is now available on AI Gateway . Gemini 4 Argon is built for coding, agentic work, and complex reasoning. It has a 1M token context window, accepts text, image, PDF, and video input, and supports tool calling. On coding tasks, Gemini 4 Argon builds features, fixes bugs, and researches unfamiliar codebases, carrying longer tasks through multiple steps. The model also reads dense diagrams, spreadsheets, layout-heavy documents, and video, which suits tasks like a financial analysis spread across several spreadsheet tabs. items.title: 手を動かして学ぶ React + TypeScript 実践入門 ― Vite で作る型安全なモダンフロントエンド（SPA）
items.summary: > 「React で実際に動くWebアプリ（SPA）を、型安全に、実務レベルで作れるようになりたい」—— 本書は、ITパスポート程度のIT知識と HTML/CSS/JavaScript の基本はあるが React・TypeScript は初めて、という人を対象に、 最初のコンポーネントから一貫して TypeScript で型を付けながら、JSX・props・状態管理（useState/useReducer/Context）・ 副作用（useEffect）・フォームとバリデーション・ルーティング（React Router）・非同期API連携・テスト（Vitest + Testing Library）・ ビルドとデプロイまでを一気通貫で身につける教材です。 動作確認用の Docker 環境（Vite + React + TypeScript）を同梱し、Windows・Mac のどちらでも同じ手順で学べます。 最終的に、API と連携する実用的な SPA を一人で設計・実装・テストできる状態を目指します。 > - JSX/TSX・関数コンポーネント・型注釈の基礎を読み書きできるようになる - props を型付きで設計し、再利用しやすいコンポーネントに分割できるようになる - useState・イベント処理・イミュータブルな状態更新を正しく扱えるようになる - リスト表示（map/key）と条件付きレンダリングをユニオン型で安全に書けるようになる - useEffect で副作用・データ取得・クリーンアップを適切に扱えるようになる - 制御コンポーネントでフォームを作り、入力検証と XSS 対策（サニタイズ）を実装できるようになる - Context と useReducer で状態を共有・集中管理できるようになる - React Router でページ遷移・動的ルート・型付き params を扱えるようになる - 非同期API連携・ローディング/エラー状態・カスタムフックを実装できるようになる - Vitest + React Testing Library でテストを書き、ESLint/Prettier・ビルド・静的ホスティングへのデプロイができるようになる
